title: Water bottles in a 5-star hotel
prompt: Please estimate the number of water bottles used in a 5-star hotel in a day.

facts.asks: Hotel size, before the candidate has named a proxy
facts.reveal: How do you generally estimate the size of a hotel?

facts.asks: Hotel size, once the candidate proposes rooms as the proxy
facts.reveal: Yes. Assume the hotel has 100 rooms.
Do you think occupancy would be constant throughout the year? What factors influence seasonality?

facts.asks: Occupancy, after the candidate has discussed seasonality
facts.reveal: Assume an average occupancy of 70% over the year.

facts.asks: Guests per occupied room, if the candidate proposes 2
Bottles per guest per day, if the candidate proposes a figure

facts.reveal: Assume the hotel has 2 restaurants. Estimate the rest.
Yes. Assume the hotel has conference facilities.

acceptedAssumptions: 2 guests per occupied room; 2 bottles per guest per day
25 tables per restaurant, 2 turns a day, 2 guests per table, 1 bottle per cover
3 conference rooms, 2 in use a day, 40 attendees per event, 1 bottle each
1.5 staff per room, so 150 staff; 1 bottle per staff member per shift

crux.statement: Demand-centre segmentation decides the grade: direct (rooms), indirect (restaurants and events) and internal (staff), with rooms as the size proxy and awareness that occupancy moves with the season.
crux.clue: "How do you generally estimate the size of a hotel?"

paths: Bottom-up by demand centre: rooms, restaurants, conferences, staff
Any structure that covers guests, food and beverage, events and staff

quant.working: The source's chain: rooms 100 × 70% × 2 × 2 = 280. Restaurants 2 × 25 × 2 × 2 = 200. Conferences 2 × 40 = 80. Staff 150 × 1 = 150. Total 710 bottles a day. Sanity check, derived: 710 ÷ 100 rooms is about 7 bottles per room, or about 10 per occupied room.
quant.answer: One reasonable result: 710 bottles a day. Grade the approach, never the distance from this figure.

answerKey: A total with its four buckets
How the figure moves in peak and lean seasons

close.condition: The candidate has totalled at least three demand buckets.
close.prompt: What's your final estimate, and which assumption matters most?

anchors.s7: All four buckets with clean maths.
anchors.s9: All buckets plus occupancy and seasonality reasoning, a sanity check, and a note on the biggest assumption.

verifierFlags.text: The summary slide lists the candidate's 1.5 staff per room as a case fact.
verifierFlags.decision: Only 100 rooms, 70% occupancy, 2 restaurants and the conference facilities are interviewer facts. Everything else is an accepted assumption.

verifierFlags.text: "1 bottle per shift" × 150 staff assumes 150 is total staff across all shifts.
verifierFlags.decision: Accepted as it stands. A top answer says so.
